2027-05-15.title: The Holy Mother of God for the ears of grain · Mar Pachomios · Saturday of the sixth week after Qyomtho
readings: The one who sows bountifully will reap bountifully; God loves a cheerful giver
“Blessed rather are those who hear the word of God and obey it!”
2027-05-15.alt: Season of Qyomtho (the Resurrection): the ten days of waiting between Suloko (the Ascension) and Pentecost, in the week after the Sixth Sunday after Qyomtho. The Panchangam keeps today the commemoration of the Holy Mother of God for the ears of grain, the memory of Mar Pachomios (St Pachomius of Egypt), and the name day of Most Rev. Mathews Mar Pachomios. Tomorrow is Pentecost.
2027-05-15.verse: Blessed rather are those who hear the word of God and obey it!
theo: On the last day before Pentecost, with the Church gathered in prayer as the apostles were gathered with Mary, the Panchangam turns our eyes to the Mother of God, and it does so in the language of the fields. Today is the commemoration of the Holy Mother of God “for the ears of grain.” In the old farming year of the Syriac lands the wheat was coming to the ear in May, and the Church brought the coming harvest to the Mother of the Lord and asked her prayers. (The Syriac calendars know other such days in the farmer's year, for the seed that is sown and for the vines; our Panchangam keeps today's.) This is not a pious decoration on the calendar. It springs from the heart of our faith. The Fathers of the Syriac Church loved to call Mary the field that was never sown, yet brought forth the Sheaf of blessing: the Virgin earth from which sprang the Bread of life. St Ephrem sings of her as the land that gave us the Wheat which feeds the world (Hymns on the Nativity, in substance). Jesus himself spoke of the grain: “unless a grain of wheat falls into the earth and dies, it remains just a single grain; but if it dies, it bears much fruit.” He was born in Bethlehem, whose name means “house of bread”; he gives himself as bread at every Holy Qurbono. When we remember the ears of grain in May, we remember the Mother who gave the world its true Bread.

The Gospel might seem at first to turn away from Mary. A woman in the crowd cries out, “Blessed is the womb that bore you and the breasts that nursed you!” And Jesus answers, “Blessed rather are those who hear the word of God and obey it!” But the Lord is not lessening his Mother; he is telling us where her true greatness lies. St Augustine says that Mary was more blessed in receiving the faith of Christ than in conceiving the flesh of Christ (On Holy Virginity 3, in substance). She was the first to hear the word and keep it: “Here am I, the servant of the Lord; let it be with me according to your word.” She “treasured all these words and pondered them in her heart.” Elizabeth had already said of her, “blessed is she who believed.” The Second Vatican Council reads this very Gospel so: when Jesus proclaimed blessed those who hear and keep the word of God, Mary was faithfully doing just that (Lumen Gentium 58). So the woman in the crowd was right, and Jesus made her blessing deeper. Every one of us can share in the blessedness of the Mother, not by bearing Christ in the flesh, but by bearing his word in a believing heart. And tonight, on the eve of Pentecost, we wait with her, who “aided the beginnings of the Church by her prayers.”

St Paul's words to the Corinthians speak the farmer's language too. He is gathering a collection for the poor Christians of Jerusalem, and he writes: “the one who sows sparingly will also reap sparingly, and the one who sows bountifully will also reap bountifully. Each of you must give as you have made up your mind, not reluctantly or under compulsion, for God loves a cheerful giver.” Then he praises the Lord of every harvest: “He who supplies seed to the sower and bread for food will supply and multiply your seed for sowing and increase the harvest of your righteousness.” The Panchangam also remembers today Mar Pachomios, St Pachomius of Egypt, who lived in the fourth century. As a young conscript held in a prison in Thebes, he was astonished when strangers came at night with bread and water for the prisoners. They were Christians. He promised God that if he were released he would serve others in the same way. He was baptised, learned the life of prayer from an old hermit, and gathered the first great communities of monks who lived, prayed, worked the land and shared everything in common. A cheerful gift of bread made a saint, and the saint made thousands of brothers. We pray today too for Most Rev. Mathews Mar Pachomios, a bishop of our Church, on his name day, that he may sow bountifully and reap a harvest of righteousness among God's people. Tomorrow the great Harvest begins: the Spirit will come down, and the apostles will gather in the first sheaves of the Church.
conn: The field that bore the Bread.
John 12:24 and John 6:35, with the Syriac Fathers: Christ the grain of wheat and the Bread of life came forth from the Virgin, the field that was never sown.
Luke 11:28 with Luke 1:38, 1:45 and 2:19: Mary is blessed above all because she heard the word of God and kept it.
2 Corinthians 9:6 with Psalm 126:5–6 and Galatians 6:9: the generous sower shares in God's own harvest.
fathers: Blessed is the Virgin earth that was never sown, yet brought forth the Sheaf of blessing; from her came the Wheat that feeds the hungry world (Hymns on the Nativity, in substance).

Mary was more blessed in receiving the faith of Christ than in conceiving the flesh of Christ; her motherhood would have profited her nothing had she not borne Christ more happily in her heart than in her flesh (On Holy Virginity 3, in substance).
magis: In the course of her Son's preaching, Mary received the words by which, raising the Kingdom above ties of flesh and blood, he proclaimed blessed those who hear and keep the word of God, as she was faithfully doing (in substance).

After her Son's Ascension, Mary aided the beginnings of the Church by her prayers; in her association with the apostles and several women, we also see Mary by her prayers imploring the gift of the Spirit.
In the beginning God entrusted the earth and its resources to the common stewardship of mankind; the goods of creation are destined for the whole human race (in substance).
outline: Ask: what harvest is God preparing in my life, and what seed am I sowing?

Tonight, on the eve of Pentecost, read Acts 1:12–14 and 2:1–4 slowly as a family, and choose one word to keep.
2027-05-15.prayer: Lord God, Father of all good gifts, you supply seed to the sower and bread for food, and from the Virgin Mary, the field that was never sown, you gave us your Son, the Bread of life. On this commemoration of the Holy Mother of God for the ears of grain, we bring you the fields of our land and the work of all who farm them; bless the coming harvest and let no one go hungry. Make us like the Mother of your Son, who heard your word and kept it, and teach us to sow bountifully and give cheerfully, as Mar Pachomios learned from the strangers who brought him bread. Bless Most Rev. Mathews Mar Pachomios on his name day, and keep him a faithful shepherd. As we wait with Mary for the coming of your Spirit, gather us into the harvest of your Kingdom. Through Christ our Lord, who with you and the Holy Spirit lives and reigns for ever. Amen.
altar: The wheat of our fields becomes the bread of the altar, and by the descent of the Holy Spirit it becomes the Body of the Lord, born of the Virgin Mother of God: the true Bread from the field that was never sown.

quick: Today the Panchangam remembers the Holy Mother of God for the ears of grain: Mary is the field that bore the Bread of life.
Jesus: blessed rather are those who hear the word of God and obey it; Mary did so first and best.
Paul: sow bountifully; God loves a cheerful giver. St Pachomius became a monk after strangers brought him bread in prison.
2027-05-15.action: Give something today, gladly, to someone who is hungry.
2027-05-15.question: Do I keep God's word in my heart as Mary did, or do I only hear it?
term: Syriac for “she who gave birth to God,” the Mother of God (Greek Theotokos). The Church confessed this title at the Council of Ephesus in 431, because the child Mary bore is the eternal Son of God made man.
kidsaint: St Pachomius and the bread in the night

Pachomius was a young soldier who was locked in a prison with other young men. One night some strangers came with bread and water for them. Pachomius asked, “Who are these kind people?” Someone told him, “They are Christians.” He was so touched that he decided to become a Christian and spend his life helping others. Later he started big homes where many monks lived, prayed and worked together. Lesson: a small kindness, like sharing food, can change someone's whole life.

family.explain: A woman in the crowd shouted that Jesus' mother was very blessed. Jesus said that people who hear God's word and do what it says are blessed too. Mother Mary did that better than anyone. Today our Church also thanks God for the grain growing in the fields, which becomes our bread.
family.intention: We pray for farmers, for the coming harvest, and for all who do not have enough to eat.
family.ask: Ask: “What can we share with someone who is hungry this week?”

illus: In a paddy village near Kuttanad, an old farmer had a custom his grandchildren found strange. When the first ears of rice appeared each season, he would cut a few stalks, tie them with a thread and take them to the parish church, where he laid them quietly before the icon of the Mother of God. “She gave us the Bread,” he would say, “so I bring her the first bread.” One year the harvest failed in the neighbouring fields because of floods, and his own was small. Still he took the first stalks to church, and afterwards he sent half his rice to the families who had lost everything. His grandson asked why he gave so much when they had so little. The old man laughed: “The one who sows bountifully reaps bountifully. Have you ever seen the Mother of God let a cheerful giver go hungry?”

pm.open: Christ is risen! Holy Mother of God, you heard the word of God and kept it, and you waited with the apostles for the Spirit. Pray for us tonight, on the eve of Pentecost. Amen.
share: Blessed rather are those who hear the word of God and obey it (Luke 11:28). Which word of God am I being asked to keep this week?
The one who sows bountifully will also reap bountifully (2 Corinthians 9:6). Where am I sowing sparingly?
He who supplies seed to the sower and bread for food (2 Corinthians 9:10). For which gifts of the harvest do I need to thank God?
interc: For the Church on the eve of Pentecost, that with Mary she may receive the Holy Spirit in fullness.
For farmers and farm workers, for the coming monsoon and the harvest, that the earth may yield its increase.
For the hungry and for all who share their bread, that God may multiply their seed.
For Most Rev. Mathews Mar Pachomios on his name day, and for all our bishops, that they may be faithful shepherds.
For monks and sisters, that like St Pachomius they may live in prayer, work and sharing.
pm.close: Father, through the Mother of God you gave us the Bread of life. Make us hear and keep your word, give cheerfully, and wait with her for your Holy Spirit. Amen.

homily: Dear friends, Christ is risen! Tomorrow is Pentecost. Today, the last day of waiting, our Church turns to the Mother of God, and she does it in a very homely way: the Panchangam calls today the commemoration of the Holy Mother of God “for the ears of grain.” In May the wheat in the old Syriac lands was coming to the ear, and the Church brought the harvest to Mary and asked her prayers. Why Mary? Because the Fathers called her the field that was never sown, from which came the Bread of life. Jesus was born in Bethlehem, which means “house of bread,” and he feeds us with his own Body at every Holy Qurbono.

In the Gospel a woman praises Jesus' Mother: “Blessed is the womb that bore you!” And Jesus says, “Blessed rather are those who hear the word of God and obey it!” Is Jesus putting his Mother down? Not at all. He is telling us the secret of her greatness. Mary was blessed because she heard God's word and said yes to it: “let it be with me according to your word.” She kept the words of God in her heart and pondered them. So we too can share her blessedness, if we hear God's word and keep it.

St Paul gives us the farmer's lesson: “the one who sows sparingly will also reap sparingly, and the one who sows bountifully will also reap bountifully... for God loves a cheerful giver.” Today we also remember Mar Pachomios, St Pachomius of Egypt. As a young soldier in prison, he was given bread by strangers in the night. They were Christians. That one act of kindness made him a Christian, and later he founded great communities of monks who prayed, worked and shared everything. We also pray today for Most Rev. Mathews Mar Pachomios, whose name day it is.

So, on the eve of Pentecost, let us do three things. Let us thank God for the harvest and pray for our farmers. Let us give something today, cheerfully, to someone in need. And let us wait with Mary, as the apostles did, for the Holy Spirit. Let us say tonight, with the Mother of God, “Here am I; let it be with me according to your word.” Then tomorrow the Spirit will find a field ready for his harvest.
kids: Children, Christ is risen! Do you know where bread comes from? From wheat, a plant that grows in fields. In May the wheat grows little heads full of grain, called ears. Today our Church thanks God for the grain, and remembers Mother Mary. Why? Because Mary gave us Jesus, who said, “I am the bread of life.” Jesus also said that the people who are really happy are those who listen to God's word and do it. Mary did that perfectly. Tomorrow is Pentecost, the birthday of the Church! Tonight, say a prayer with your family: “Mother Mary, help us to listen to Jesus. Come, Holy Spirit!”

intro: Theme: “Blessed rather are those who hear the word of God and obey it!”

On the commemoration of the Holy Mother of God for the ears of grain and the memory of Mar Pachomios, on the eve of Pentecost: the field that bore the Bread, the blessedness of hearing and keeping, and the cheerful giver.

points.h: The field that bore the Bread
sub: The ears of grain in May.
The Virgin earth and the Bread of life.
q: The Lord will give what is good, and our land will yield its increase.
Very truly, I tell you, unless a grain of wheat falls into the earth and dies, it remains just a single grain; but if it dies, it bears much fruit.
points.apply: Thank God for your daily bread at each meal today, and pray a Hail Mary for farmers.

sub: Mary, the first to hear and keep.
Waiting with her for the Spirit.
q: I treasure your word in my heart, so that I may not sin against you.
But Mary treasured all these words and pondered them in her heart.
points.apply: Choose one verse from tomorrow's Pentecost readings and keep it in your heart all week.

sub: Bread given in a prison at night.
q: May those who sow in tears reap with shouts of joy.
So let us not grow weary in doing what is right, for we will reap at harvest time, if we do not give up.
points.apply: Give food or money to someone in need before tomorrow's Holy Qurbono, gladly and without counting.

concl: The Mother of God is the field that gave the world its Bread; her true blessedness is the word heard and kept.
On the eve of Pentecost we wait with her, sowing bountifully, for the Spirit who brings in God's harvest.
2027-05-15.resolve: Hear God's word and keep it as Mary did, give cheerfully, and wait with her for the Holy Spirit.
